q: In an ecosystem, green plants that photosynthesise to produce food are called ______.
e: Producers are defined as green plants that photosynthesise to produce food.

q: Animals that eat plants or other animals are known as ______.
e: The textbook defines consumers as animals that eat plants or other animals.

q: Organisms that break down dead material and help to recycle nutrients are called ______.
e: Decomposers are described as organisms that break down dead material and recycle nutrients; they are also termed reducers.

q: Abiotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT ______.
e: Predation is a biotic factor; temperature and soil pH are abiotic factors listed in the text.

q: Biotic factors include all of the following EXCEPT ______.
e: Salinity is an abiotic factor; the others are biotic interactions mentioned in the textbook.

q: All the organisms of a particular species found in an ecosystem at a certain time form a ______.
e: The textbook defines a population as all organisms of a particular species in an ecosystem at a given time.

q: The populations of all species found in an ecosystem at a particular time form the ______.
e: A community is defined as the collection of all populations of different species in an ecosystem at a given time.

q: In a food chain, the arrow (→) means ______.
e: The textbook explicitly states that in a food chain, the arrow means 'is eaten by'.

q: The different stages in a food chain (producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer) are called ______.
e: These stages are defined as trophic levels in section 6.2.1.

q: A food web shows feeding relationships with ______.
e: The textbook explains that a food web illustrates feeding relationships across different food chains in an ecosystem.
